title: Solve a modulus equation by splitting into cases
content: When an equation contains |expression| set equal to something else, split into two separate equations: one where the expression inside the modulus is taken as positive (remove the bars as-is) and one where it is taken as negative (remove the bars and negate the expression). Solve each resulting equation for x, then check both solutions actually satisfy the original equation (since squaring or case-splitting can introduce extraneous roots) — reject any that don't. This is often faster and safer than squaring both sides, which can create a higher-degree equation.
